items.notes: Quote: 'A controlled consumer can no longer stop internal handling with preventDefault() or details.cancel()' ... 'now clears the Form server error and runs validate, where the base code skipped both.' The register non_defect rules that the missing react#9023 defaultPrevented guard on the controlled path has 'no demonstrated failure', because the controlled path no longer depends on the DOM event. For cancel, the scenario has the consumer call d.cancel() and still setV(next). Controlled state then really changed, and useValueChanged syncs from the value prop by design, matching sibling controls. The asserted regression lacks support.

Quote: 'The field becomes data-dirty and markedDirtyRef is set, so it can never read pristine again ... a form-library reset(newValues) leaves the field permanently dirty.' Programmatic changes updating dirty and validity is the PR's stated purpose. The register non_defect 'Programmatic value changes in onChange mode now trigger validation (e.g. form-library population)' is ruled promised with no demonstrated harm. 'Never read pristine again' is wrong: markedDirtyRef is used only for valueMissing suppression (useFieldValidation.ts:225). data-dirty is recomputed as serializedValue !== initialValue on every change (FieldControl.tsx:111), so it clears when the value returns to baseline.

Quote: '<Field.Control value={null} onValueChange={...} /> (common from nullable form models) is treated as controlled ... Dirty, filled and on-change validation never update'. value is typed from React input props (string | readonly string[] | number | undefined via BaseUIComponentProps<'input'>), and null is outside that type. React itself warns on value={null}. The register non_defect on the serializedValue === undefined skip rules null/undefined handling outside the contract. No supported usage is shown to fail.

Quote: 'onChange mode now costs an extra render per keystroke ... The effect also lets a frame paint with stale data-dirty, data-filled and aria-invalid.' The extra render is the documented trade-off (register non_defect, PR Performance table). The stale-paint consequence is refuted: the sync runs in useValueChanged's useIsoLayoutEffect (useValueChanged.ts:10), which flushes synchronously before paint. The register non_defect also rules the 'visual flash or tearing' claim hypothetical.

Quote: 'When details.cancel() is called in uncontrolled mode, setDirty and setFilled still run. Only clearErrors and validation.change are skipped.' Accurate (FieldControl.tsx:148-156). In uncontrolled mode the DOM keeps the typed text, so dirty and filled are truthful. The 'inconsistent' consequence is the promised effect of cancel skipping validation. Below the threshold.

Quote: 'The new tests never check the promised behaviors ... No test covers value={null}, arrays, rejected controlled updates'. A test-coverage and hygiene remark; the register rules the render-count test naming non-material. The 'unhandled paths above' it relies on are not registered defects.

Quote: 'In uncontrolled mode details.cancel() only skips clearErrors and validation.change. setDirty and setFilled still run'. Accurate (FieldControl.tsx:148-156), but dirty and filled truthfully follow the uncontrolled DOM value. Skipping validation and error clearing is the promised effect of cancel. Below the threshold.

Quote: 'The controlled path returns early from onChange and drops the event.nativeEvent.defaultPrevented guard ... Now the useValueChanged effect validates and clears errors anyway.' Register non_defect: 'The react#9023 defaultPrevented workaround no longer guards the controlled path' — the controlled path no longer depends on the DOM change event; no demonstrated failure. The consumer in the scenario still updates the value, so syncing is by design.

Quote: 'useValueChanged returns early when serializedValue becomes undefined ... A form-library reset sets the control's value from 'abc' to null or undefined ... data-filled and data-dirty stay set'. This is the register non_defect directly: 'clearing a controlled value to undefined/null is ignored' is ruled outside the contract, because undefined means uncontrolled and null is not a valid input value type.

Quote: 'The mount effect no longer clears filled for an empty controlled value. The old effect called setFilled(false) when valueProp === '', and useValueChanged does nothing on first mount' ... 'Field.Control is conditionally unmounted and remounted with value='' ... data-filled stays wrong'. This is exactly GT-r2 manifestation (1), with the correct mechanism at FieldControl.tsx:99-103, so it is a recovery. No change is proposed, so fix_sufficiency is absent.

Quote: 'Any controlled value change now marks the field dirty ... runs validation, including async prefill ... The user sees errors on a field they never touched ... The PR body does not call it out'. The PR body calls it out explicitly ('Setting the value from code, such as a clear button or a form library reset ... updated the input text but not filled, dirty, or validity'). Register non_defect: programmatic changes in onChange mode triggering validation is promised, with no demonstrated harm. The valueMissing consequence cannot arise from a prefill to a non-empty value. The item also does not tie normalisation to blur, so it is not GT-r1.

Quote: 'The registered baseline and value now use String(value). An object or array value becomes '[object Object]' or 'a,b' ... not documented for non-string values.' Register non_defect: String(value) serialization is intended, because the DOM value is always a string. The DOM shows the same 'a,b' either way. The item's consequence is mild, a documentation note.

Quote: 'goes from 1 to 2 renders per keystroke, as the PR body admits'. Register non_defect: a documented, measured trade-off that matches Number Field. The note about the missing onChange-mode render test is hygiene.
Quote: 'There are no tests for the PR's other claims ... renders once per keystroke is misnamed'. A test-coverage and naming remark; the register rules the brittle render test non-material.
Quote: 'The autoFocus layout effect and the inputRef declaration were moved below the new hooks. This is unrelated churn'. A diff-hygiene remark with no demonstrated behavioural consequence.

Quote: 'The early return for controlled inputs skips the event.nativeEvent.defaultPrevented and details.isCanceled guards ... The server error is now cleared and validate runs ... nothing catches this regression.' Register non_defect: the react#9023 guard no longer covering the controlled path has 'no demonstrated failure'. In the scenario the consumer still calls setValue, so controlled state changed and syncing from the value prop is the design, as in sibling controls. For cancel, the item concedes it works when the consumer does not update state, which is the controlled contract.

Quote: 'In uncontrolled mode, details.cancel() skips validation but setDirty and setFilled still run.' Accurate (FieldControl.tsx:148-156). The uncontrolled DOM keeps the text, so dirty and filled are truthful, and keeping errors and skipping validation is what cancel promises. Below the threshold.

Quote: 'When the controlled value becomes null (or undefined) ... filled, dirty, and validity are never updated ... A consumer clears the field with setValue(null)'. This is the register non_defect directly: 'useValueChanged skips serializedValue === undefined, so clearing a controlled value to undefined/null is ignored', which is outside the contract. The input value type also excludes null.

Quote: 'The old effect re-ran on every valueProp change and also called setFilled(false) for valueProp === ''. The new effect runs once ... The controlled path depends entirely on useValueChanged, which does not fire when the value is unchanged.' This names GT-r2's mechanism: the removed valueProp branch (FieldControl.tsx:99-103), with mount-time controlled filled no longer derived from the prop because useValueChanged does not fire on mount. A reader would act on it by restoring that derivation. The scenarios given are weak: uncontrolled autofill after mount is not a regression, since the merge-base effect did not re-run for it either, and the 'DOM briefly non-empty' controlled mount is vague. The item misses the concrete remount and custom-element cases, but it is a borderline recovery. No change is proposed, so absent.

Quote: 'Every programmatic controlled change runs clearErrors(name) ... a server error set via <Form errors> is cleared on a plain rerender that merely changes the value. A user who types, has the consumer reject the change ... gets no touched or validation feedback'. Register non_defects: clearErrors on programmatic changes is promised (the same already happened on every keystroke), and a consumer-rejected or rewritten value not reaching field state is promised, matching Combobox, Number Field and OTP Field. The normalisation example is on change, not blur, so it is not GT-r1.

Quote: 'The PR body concedes this: 2 renders per keystroke in onChange mode, up from 1.' Register non_defect: a documented, measured trade-off matching Number Field. The alternative design suggestion is non-material.

Quote: 'There are no tests for the new controlled-mode edge cases: consumer rejects or rewrites the value, details.cancel() when controlled, a controlled event that is default-prevented, array values, or a null value.' A test-coverage remark. The 'regression' it cites (controlled defaultPrevented) is a register non_defect.

Quote: 'a controlled non-string value ... reaches the Form-submit-time validate as a string, matching what the change and blur paths already pass'. True (FieldControl.tsx:86 serializedValue registered), and the item states it as a neutral observation. Register non_defect: submit-time serialized string is 'consistency, no demonstrated failure'.

Quote: 'In the uncontrolled path details.cancel() skips error clearing and validation but dirty and filled still follow the DOM value, and the controlled value-driven sync does not consult cancellation.' Accurate: FieldControl.tsx:148-156 calls setDirty/setFilled before the isCanceled check, and useValueChanged has no cancel check. It is a neutral observation. In uncontrolled mode the DOM really holds the typed text, so dirty/filled matching it is not harmful. No material consequence is asserted.

Quote: 'The controlled path no longer applies the defaultPrevented guard, and the only test for prevented changes is uncontrolled.' Accurate observation with no consequence asserted. Register non_defect: the react#9023 guard no longer protecting the controlled path has 'no demonstrated failure'.

Quote: 'the validate argument on the submit-time path and validityData.value/initialValue are now the serialized string (for example "5" instead of 5), matching what the change path already passed.' Accurate, neutral observation. Register non_defect: consistency change with no demonstrated failure.

Quote: 'The claims that a consumer-rejected or rewritten controlled value never reaches field state, and that array values serialize, have no dedicated test in the change; scratch probes at head show both hold.' A test-coverage observation that asserts no defect.

Quote: 'The uncontrolled path still sets dirty and filled after details.cancel(); only validation and error clearing are skipped.' Accurate (FieldControl.tsx:148-156), neutral, with no consequence. dirty and filled truthfully follow the uncontrolled DOM.

Quote: 'The merge-base mount effect called setFilled(false) for a controlled '', this change deleted that branch, and useValueChanged cannot fire on mount' ... 'The Field.Root keeps data-filled although the mounted input is empty'. This is GT-r2 manifestation (1), the controlled remount-empty case, with the exact mechanism (FieldControl.tsx:99-103 and the removed valueProp branch), so it is a recovery. Proposed fix: setFilled(Boolean(inputRef.current?.value)) in the mount effect when controlled. That clears the stale filled state for the remount case. It still reads the DOM, though, so a controlled value on render={<div/>} (manifestation 2: inputRef.value undefined) still never sets filled. The required outcome is to derive filled from the value prop independently of the element. Partial.

Quote: 'In uncontrolled mode a canceled change skips error clearing and validation but still updates dirty and filled, which follow the DOM value.' Accurate (FieldControl.tsx:148-156). The DOM does hold the typed value in uncontrolled mode, so dirty/filled reflecting it is correct state. This is an observation below the threshold.

Quote: 'A programmatic reset of a controlled required field to '' in onChange mode clears data-dirty and data-filled but shows the valueMissing error, because markedDirtyRef stays true.' Plausibly accurate: markedDirtyRef suppresses valueMissing only while false (useFieldValidation.ts:225), and FieldRoot/registration set it true on dirty. The item states it neutrally, with no fix. The register non_defect 'Programmatic value changes in onChange mode now trigger validation' is ruled promised with no demonstrated harm, and the same error would show had the user cleared the field. Below the threshold.
